Lean Hog (/HE) Market Outlook & News

Current Date: February 6, 2026

The market enters the second weekend of February with futures showing resilience despite a slight mid-week pullback. The "Winter Storm Paradox" remains a critical narrative as slaughter numbers, while recovering from January lows, continue to lag behind 2025 levels. As the February contract (HEG26) approaches its February 13th expiration, the market is aggressively pivoting toward the spring contracts, supported by a significant jump in belly prices and stabilizing grain costs.

Market Intelligence: The New Trade Map

The "Efficiency Paradox" is now a global phenomenon. While the U.S. manages disease and weather, our competitors and customers are shifting their strategies:

China’s Domestic Record: China reported record pork production of 59.38 million tons for 2025. Consequently, their imports have plummeted nearly 78% compared to 2020 levels. They are currently targeting a further reduction of 1 million sows to rebalance their oversupplied domestic market.
The Brazil Surge: Brazil has solidified its position as the world’s third-largest exporter. They are aggressively capturing market share in the Philippines (projected up 7% in 2026) and Mexico, often at the expense of U.S. and EU market share due to their low-cost production model.
EU Trade Friction: Spain, a major EU producer, is facing ASF-related trade bans from Japan and the Philippines. This, combined with China's anti-dumping duties on EU pork, is forcing European supply to stay within the continent, potentially depressing global prices if that supply isn't absorbed.

1. Supply & Demand: The Tug-of-War

Production and Slaughter: USDA estimated federally inspected hog slaughter for Thursday at 450,000 head, bringing the week-to-date total to 1.897 million. While this is higher than the previous week, it remains 3.6% below the same period last year, signaling that the supply side remains tighter than seasonal averages.

Inventory Depletion: Frozen pork stocks remain the primary bullish driver. With the lowest levels in decades, any disruption in slaughter—such as the recently authorized JBS union strike action—could trigger immediate volatility in the carcass cutout.
2. The "Disease Floor" & Logistics

Health Alert: PRRSV case positivity remains a structural concern at 48.5% in wean-to-market data. This persistent disease pressure is preventing the "record production" forecast from fully materializing on the hook, providing a firm floor for the April and May contracts.

Strike Risk: The Feb 6 news of authorized strike action at JBS facilities adds a new layer of logistical risk. If realized, this could bottleneck the pipeline, temporarily supporting futures as the market anticipates a reduction in available retail supply.
3. Export Velocity & Demand

Mexico's Dominance: The Feb 5 Export Sales report confirmed Mexico as the top buyer, taking 13,800 MT of the 35,100 MT sold for the week. While total net sales were down 37% week-over-week, physical shipments remain strong at 37,600 MT.

Belly Price Surge: Demand for bacon is providing massive support to the cutout. In the most recent reports, belly prices surged over $6.00, driving the overall carcass value back toward the mid-$90s.
Technical Forecast: Monday Open (Feb 9)

Bullish Case: February Hogs (HEG26) settled near $87.30. A break back above 88.85 is needed to signal a run at the 90.00 level before expiration next Friday.

Bearish Case: If the cash-futures convergence drags futures lower, look for technical support at 86.00, aligning with the CME Index's steady climb.

Commitment of Traders: Managed money has further expanded its net long position to 113,806 contracts, a massive vote of institutional confidence in a spring rally.
Current Crush Dynamics (February 6, 2026)
Profit margins for producers have improved as April and May futures hold their gains while corn prices faced significant pressure on Friday.

In view of the Sri Kattamaisamma Jathara at Suraram, falling within the jurisdiction of the Jeedimetla Traffic Police Station, traffic restrictions will be in force for two days from 08.02.2026 at 05:00 hours to 09.02.2026 at 23:30 hours. 

During this period, all heavy vehicle commuters are requested to use the routes mentioned below in order to avoid traffic congestion.

To facilitate smooth conduct of Kattamaisamma Jathara, certain measures to regulate traffic at various places/junctions/roads need to be taken.

RESTRICTION OF HEAVY VEHICLES:

1) The traffic (Heavy Vehicles) coming from Balanagar towards Gandimaisamma will be diverted at JETL – Industrial area – Dulapally road – Left turn – Bahadurpally X road – Gandimaisamma.
2) The traffic (Heavy Vehicles) coming from Gandimaisamma X road to Balanagar will be diverted at Bahadurpally jn – Dulapally village jn – Right turn – Industrial area – JETL Kaman – Shapurnagar – Balanagar.

Hence, the general public are requested to consider the above advisory and plan accordingly and are requested to co-operate with Traffic Police in ensuring free flow of traffic.
